We have template info. The mapped_rxn shows product? It seems forward reaction: precursors -> product. The product SMILES likely is first part before ">>"? Actually mapped_rxn: '[CH3:1][CH:2](CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)[C:4]1=[CH:5][C:6](Br)=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH:9]1.[Li]CCCC.CC[O:3]CC>>[CH3:1][C:2](=[O:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH:9]1'

So product SMILES: '[CH3:1][C:2](=[O:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH:9]1' which is a benzoyl? Let's convert to SMILES without mapping: CH3-C(=O)-c1=... Actually [CH3][C](=O)[c]... So product is something like "CC(=O)c1cccc(Br)c1"? Wait the aromatic ring has Br? The precursor aromatic had Br attached. The product after acylation loses Br? In Friedel-Crafts acylation, halide leaves? Actually acyl chloride adds acyl group, halide leaves. Here product likely is the acylated aromatic without Br. The precursor aromatic is bromobenzene attached to side chain? The precursor list from earlier: apply_template-2 gave precursors: ["CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)c1cccc(Br)c1", "CCOCC"] So product is target molecule: combine those to get product SMILES. So target SMILES is likely "CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)c1cccc(C(=O)CCOCC)c1"? Wait acyl group is CCOCC? Actually second precursor is "CCOCC" which is ethoxy ethane? That's maybe the acyl fragment? Actually Friedel-Crafts acylation uses acyl chloride, but here maybe using "CCOCC" as acyl source? The mapped_rxn shows CC[O:3]CC as part of precursor (maybe ethoxy group). The product has C(=O) attached to aromatic. So product SMILES: "CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)c1cccc(C(=O)CCOCC)c1"? But the carbonyl attached directly to aromatic, not with ethoxy? Wait C(=O) attached to aromatic, and the carbonyl carbon is attached to O-CH2CH3? Actually the precursor "CC[O:3]CC" is an ether? That seems like O attached to carbonyl? The mapping shows O atom is part of carbonyl: [C:2](=[O:3])... So O is double bonded to carbonyl, not ether. So the precursor "CC[O:3]CC" is maybe "CCOCC" which is a diethyl ether? But O is double bonded in product, so the precursor must be something like "CC(=O)CC"? Actually "CC[O:3]CC" with O as atom 3, but mapping may be ambiguous. Probably the acyl fragment is "CCOCC" which is maybe "CH3-CH2-O-CH2-CH3"? That doesn't make sense for acyl. Could be "CH3-CH2-CO-CH2-CH3"? That SMILES is "CC(=O)CC". But they gave "CCOCC". Might be missing =. Anyway we can trust the product SMILES from mapped_rxn: remove mapping numbers and brackets: "[CH3][C](=O)[c]1=...". Let's generate: CH3C(=O)c1=... The aromatic part: c1=[CH][CH]=[CH][CH]=[CH]1 corresponds to a phenyl ring with one substituent (the carbonyl) and a Br? Actually the Br was on precursor aromatic, but product no Br. So product SMILES: "CC(=O)c1cccc(c1)??" plus the side chain attached to aromatic at position? The side chain is "CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)" attached to aromatic at some position. In precursor aromatic: "CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)c1cccc(Br)c1". So aromatic has side chain at position 1, Br at another. After acylation, Br replaced by acyl group (C(=O)CCOCC). So product SMILES: "CC(CN1CCCCC1CC1CCCCC1)c1cccc(C(=O)CCOCC)c1". That seems plausible.

Thus we can construct route JSON: root molecule with SMILES target. It has two children: reaction node with template_id 23352, children are two precursor molecules with SMILES as above list.

We need to verify step using verify_step. Let's call verify_step with target SMILES, template_id 23352, precursors list.
